name: Closet Count
shortDescription: Every garment a swatch, every outfit a card, cost per wear that falls.
description: A wardrobe page for the clothes you actually wear. It opens with your whole closet sliding into a strip of paint chips sorted by color, then the closet settles below it by kind: tops, bottoms, dresses, layers, shoes, bags, and accessories, each a tinted silhouette with what it now costs per wear. Your outfits hang on a rack you flick through, each laid out flat with its layers drifting as the card passes. One tap while you get dressed marks an outfit or a single piece worn today: its cost per wear rolls down and its ring fills toward thirty wears, closing with a small pop when it gets there. Anything you have not worn in ninety days fades a little more each week and lands on the Dusty shelf, where you keep it or give it away. The capsule shows this season's chosen pieces as one tight grid under a big count. Add pieces, stack new outfits one per slot, filter by color and season, and export or import the whole closet from Settings. It works on a phone and a laptop, needs no account, and keeps every tap in the browser you use.
setup: Your agent asks, in one message, what currency you use, walks through what is in your closet that you actually wear (each piece with its color and roughly what it cost, skipping anything you don't know), and whether you want it light or dark. It writes that into your project and builds the page. After that you tap what you wear each day; no account or key is needed.
